atoms.reason: Strong, A+B consensus architectural invariant. Keeping the planner advisory-only with a single execution chokepoint (the existing 5-gate loop) cleanly separates reasoning from actuation, maximizes reuse of proven machinery, and concentrates all safety enforcement at one auditable point. Low reversibility is acceptable because it is the correct foundational decision; test is concrete and verifiable via contract inspection.

penalties: Minor wording ambiguity: 'pauses before any atomic actions are generated' can be read as reviewing an atomic-action plan, colliding with atom_03/atom_09 (-0.03)
atoms.reason: Triple-consensus Discuss-First gate is high-value operator-safety control. Accept the intent but apply the reviewer fix: explicitly state PROJECT_PLAN is a HIGH-LEVEL plan of steps/sub-goals (not atomic actions) so it reconciles with just-in-time compilation (atom_03) and closed-loop replanning (atom_09). Specificity docked for the granularity ambiguity that the fix resolves.

A+B consensus. Just-in-time, one-step-at-a-time compilation is the natural execution model that makes closed-loop replanning (atom_09) and per-node verification (atom_04) coherent, and avoids stale pre-baked plans. Slight simplicity cost from JIT machinery, but it reduces brittleness; test is directly observable.

Triple-consensus and the safety backbone: explicit postconditions plus a bounded recovery ladder with a hard halt-on-unverified rule is exactly the 'never assume success' discipline an OS-acting agent needs. High implementation cost and added per-node complexity lower feasibility/simplicity, but the risk-reduction and impact justify it.

Triple-consensus. Elevating vision from mere element-location to grounding, anomaly detection, postcondition verification, and read-only scouting is what makes postconditions (atom_04) trustworthy. Lower feasibility/simplicity reflect genuine cost and vision-reliability concerns across four roles, but the closed-loop perception coverage is high-impact and well specified.

Highest-scoring atom. A deterministic allow/confirm/deny policy gate the LLM cannot override, with fail-closed defaults on unknowns, is the single most important safety lever — 'LLM proposes, policy disposes.' Cheap relative to its protection, highly specific, and directly testable. Strong triple-consensus.

Triple-consensus. Multi-layered STOP (operator kill-switch + automatic triggers) checked at every gate and defined as safe-freeze-and-report is essential containment. Defining STOP as freeze-and-report rather than silent abort is the key correctness nuance. High cost and the complexity of wiring triggers into every gate reduce feasibility/simplicity, but risk-reduction is maximal.

Single-source (A) but a coherent, low-cost unifying principle that generalizes the fail-closed behavior already implied by atom_04/06/07 across ambiguity, missing state, failed verification, risk escalation, and vision disagreement. Specificity slightly lower as a principle rather than a mechanism, but it closes gaps the consensus atoms leave implicit.

penalties: High-impact conflict with atom_02 over plan-generation strategy; must be scoped to operate only after high-level plan approval (-0.03)
atoms.reason: Closed-loop interleaved planning is the right runtime strategy and underpins atom_03/04/05. Modify rather than accept: the conflict matrix flags a high-impact clash with atom_02 — reconcile by scoping closed-loop replanning to the post-approval execution of the high-level PROJECT_PLAN, so Discuss-First and interleaved sense-plan-act-verify-replan coexist. Lower simplicity/feasibility from the runtime control complexity and high cost.

Single-source (B) but a critical security invariant for any vision/OCR-driven agent: treating perceived screen content as untrusted data (never instructions), keeping goal/policy in a privileged channel, and fencing to an app/target allowlist directly defends against prompt-injection via the screen. High correctness and risk-reduction; modest implementation cost.

Single-source (B), low-cost and highly reversible deployment discipline. Phased, additive rollout with human-in-loop at every risk rung and full plan-to-action provenance is the safe path to broadening autonomy. Impact and specificity are slightly lower (process/strategy rather than core mechanism), but it cheaply de-risks the whole rollout.

penalties: Tension with atom_03/atom_09: pre-generating DAG 'loop-action sequences' leans open-loop and risks stale plans (-0.02)
atoms.reason: Single-source (C). An LLM task decomposer producing a dependency-aware TaskGraph is a useful, specific mechanism, but as stated it pre-bakes 'loop-action sequences' which leans open-loop and tensions with just-in-time compilation (atom_03) and closed-loop replanning (atom_09). Modify: keep the DAG at the level of high-level steps/sub-goals (dependencies only), and defer atomic-action sequences to JIT compilation per step. High cost and DAG complexity lower feasibility/simplicity.
